chunks: And my father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from his father, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah has assigned to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) seventy thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, weeping over him until the Day of Judgment. They pray at his grave; one prayer of theirs is equal to one thousand prayers of humans. The reward of their prayers and the merit thereof will be for whoever visits his grave.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) according to the angels' prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmic significance of Karbala, where seventy thousand angels with disheveled hair weep for Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) until the Day of Judgment. Each angelic prayer equals a thousand human prayers, and this immense reward is transferred to visitors, underscoring the grave as a focal point of divine mercy and intercession in Shia piety.
